summary: The SIS Act is the principal Commonwealth law regulating superannuation entities. Part 6 deems the governing rules of every registrable superannuation entity to contain covenants binding each trustee (s52) and each director of a corporate trustee (s52A): to act honestly, with the care, skill and diligence of a prudent superannuation trustee, and in the best financial interests of beneficiaries; to manage conflicts; and to formulate and give effect to investment, insurance, risk management and retirement income strategies and annual outcomes assessments. Contravening a s52 or s52A covenant is a civil penalty provision (s54B).

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities
clauses.heading: Covenants deemed to be in governing rules (overview)
clauses.text: If the governing rules of a registrable superannuation entity do not contain covenants to the effect of those set out in s52, the rules are taken to contain them. The covenants bind each trustee of the entity and are grouped as general (s52(2)), investment (s52(6)), insurance (s52(7)), risk (s52(8)), retirement income (s52(8A)), annual outcomes assessment (s52(9)), promoting financial interests (s52(12)) and MySuper (s52(13)) covenants.
subclauses: Civil and criminal consequences follow from ss54B, 54C, 55 and 202.
Civil consequences can arise whether or not the act or omission was intentional; criminal consequences under s202 require proof of dishonesty or intention.
clauses.notes: Start here for trustee duties; look up the subsection clauses for detail.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities: General covenants
clauses.heading: General trustee covenants
clauses.text: Each trustee must: act honestly in all matters concerning the entity; exercise the care, skill and diligence a prudent superannuation trustee would exercise; perform its duties and exercise its powers in the best financial interests of beneficiaries; prioritise beneficiaries' interests where there is a conflict; treat classes of beneficiaries, and beneficiaries within a class, fairly; keep the entity's assets separate from the trustee's and employer-sponsors' assets; not enter into arrangements that hinder proper performance of its functions; manage any reserves under a prudential strategy; and give beneficiaries access to prescribed information and documents.
subclauses: (b) care, skill and diligence of a prudent superannuation trustee (defined in s52(3))
(d) conflicts: give priority to beneficiaries, ensure duties are met and interests not adversely affected despite the conflict, and comply with the prudential standards on conflicts
(e) and (f) fairness between and within classes of beneficiaries
(h) no contracts that hinder the trustee
(i) strategy for the prudential management of reserves
(j) access to prescribed information and documents
clauses.notes: Section 52(4) gives the conflicts covenant priority over certain duties of officers and employees under Corporations Act Part 2D.1 and the PGPA Act.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities: General covenants
clauses.heading: Best financial interests of beneficiaries
clauses.text: Each trustee must perform its duties and exercise its powers in the best financial interests of the beneficiaries. Section 52(3A) confirms this covenant applies to payments made to a third party by, or on behalf of, the entity.
clauses.notes: SPS 515 paragraphs 21 and 22 add prudential requirements for expenditure decisions made against this duty.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities: Investment covenants
clauses.heading: Investment covenants
clauses.text: Each trustee must formulate, regularly review and give effect to an investment strategy for the whole entity and for each investment option, having regard to risk and likely return, diversification, liquidity, the availability of reliable valuation information, the entity's ability to meet liabilities, tax consequences, costs and any other relevant matter. Trustees must also exercise due diligence in developing, offering and reviewing each investment option and ensure the options offered allow adequate diversification.
subclauses: (a)(i) to (viii) matters the investment strategy must have regard to
clauses.notes: SPS 530 sets the prudential requirements for giving effect to this covenant.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities: Insurance covenants
clauses.heading: Insurance covenants
clauses.text: Each trustee must formulate, regularly review and give effect to an insurance strategy covering the kinds and levels of cover offered, the basis for offering them having regard to the membership's demographics, and how insurers are chosen. The trustee must consider the cost of cover to all beneficiaries, only offer cover whose cost does not inappropriately erode retirement income, and do everything reasonable to pursue an insurance claim for a beneficiary that has a reasonable prospect of success.
subclauses: (c) no inappropriate erosion of retirement income
(d) pursue claims with a reasonable prospect of success
clauses.notes: Relevant where a superannuation member service or agent handles insured benefit claims.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities: Covenants relating to risk
clauses.heading: Risk management covenants
clauses.text: Each trustee must formulate, regularly review and give effect to a risk management strategy covering the trustee's relevant activities and the risks of operating the entity, and must maintain and manage, in accordance with the prudential standards, financial resources (trustee capital, an entity reserve or both) to cover the entity's operational risk.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities: Retirement income covenants
clauses.heading: Retirement income strategy covenants
clauses.text: Each trustee must formulate, regularly review and give effect to a retirement income strategy meeting s52AA, take reasonable steps to gather the information needed for it, record it in writing together with its determinations, significant decisions and reasons, and publish a summary on the entity's website. Section 52(8B) excludes funds that provide only death, permanent incapacity or temporary incapacity benefits.
clauses.notes: The content requirements in s52AA are not paraphrased in this corpus. SPS 515 paragraph 10 requires review of the strategy at least every three years.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities: Annual outcomes assessments
clauses.heading: Annual outcomes assessment
clauses.text: For a regulated superannuation fund with more than 6 members, each trustee must determine in writing each year, for each MySuper and choice product, whether the financial interests of the beneficiaries holding the product are being promoted, having regard to comparisons with other products and benchmarks, the factors in s52(11) and the latest APRA performance test determination under s60C(2).
subclauses: s52(11) factors include whether options, benefits and facilities, the investment strategy and the insurance strategy are appropriate to those beneficiaries, and whether insurance fees inappropriately erode their retirement income.
clauses.notes: SPS 515 paragraphs 27 to 29 set how the methodology must be documented and calculated.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities: Promoting financial interests
clauses.heading: Promoting financial interests of beneficiaries
clauses.text: For a regulated superannuation fund with more than 6 members, each trustee must promote the financial interests of beneficiaries holding a MySuper or choice product, in particular returns after fees, costs and taxes.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities
clauses.heading: Covenants binding directors of corporate trustees
clauses.text: Where a trustee of a registrable superannuation entity is a body corporate, the governing rules are taken to contain covenants by each director to act honestly, to exercise the care, skill and diligence of a prudent superannuation entity director, to perform duties and exercise powers in the best financial interests of beneficiaries, and to give beneficiaries' interests priority in conflicts and comply with the prudential standards on conflicts, among other covenants.
clauses.notes: Only the opening covenants of s52A(2) were read; the list is not complete here.

clauses.section_name: Part 6: Provisions relating to governing rules of superannuation entities
clauses.heading: Contravening s52 and s52A covenants is a civil penalty provision
clauses.text: A person must not contravene a covenant to the effect of a s52 or s52A covenant contained, or taken to be contained, in the governing rules. These are civil penalty provisions (s193), so Part 21 provides civil and criminal consequences. A contravention does not invalidate a transaction, and loss or damage may be recovered under s55. Section 54C separately prohibits contravening any other covenant, which is not an offence.
